VIDEO.title: The Forgotten Lesson of the Cross
VIDEO.series: The Gospel of Matthew Every Word (playlist of 58 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Matthew 27 · Episode 54 (#57 of 58 in the playlist)
hand: He showed them how to die
SUMMARY: The teacher reads all of Matthew 27. Jesus is delivered to Pilate. Judas, remorseful, returns the thirty pieces of silver, throws them into the sanctuary and hangs himself; the chief priests buy the Potter's Field. Jesus is silent before Pilate. The crowd, persuaded by the chief priests and elders, chooses Barabbas; Pilate washes his hands; 'His blood be on us and on our children!' Jesus is scourged, mocked, and crucified at Golgotha between two robbers. Darkness falls; He cries, 'My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?' and yields up His spirit. The veil is torn, the earth shakes, saints are raised, and the centurion confesses Him. Joseph of Arimathea buries Him, and the tomb is sealed and guarded.

Observations: Matthew follows the blood money to show fulfillment of Jeremiah. A commentator notes a triad who shed innocent blood: Judas (27:4), Pilate (27:24) and the crowd led by its leaders (27:25). 'You yourself say it' means 'that's your way of putting it.' Some manuscripts call Barabbas 'Jesus Barabbas'; his name means 'son of a father.' The crowd's words fit Jesus' teaching on 'this evil generation' (12:45; 23:36) and give no warrant for blaming all Jews for all time.

Jesus refuses the wine mixed with gall (myrrh in Mark 15:23). His cry is a hint pointing hearers to all of Psalm 22: He is still teaching as He dies. The video is honest about open questions: which veil was torn, and how to read the raised saints.

Connections: Deuteronomy 23:18 and the temple treasury; Zechariah 11:12-13 and Exodus 21:32; Jeremiah 19:1-13; Isaiah 53:7 and 53:9; Leviticus 20:9; Matthew 20:18-19; Proverbs 31:6; Psalm 69:21; Psalm 22; Joel 2:10; 1 Peter 2:24.
The lesson: dying is the final act of obedience that a person can perform unto God, and the one who is filled with the word of God will glorify God in their final act of obedience.
QUOTES: Dying is the final act of obedience that a person can perform unto God. And the one who is filled with the word of God will glorify God in their final act of obedience.
Jesus didn't just die for his followers. He showed them how to die.
We never outgrow these teachings, ladies and gentlemen. We only grow further and further into them.
God does not forsake his own. He did not forsake Jesus and he will not forsake his people.

LSB_QUOTES.text: And Jesus cried out again with a loud voice, and yielded up His spirit.
For He has not despised and He has not abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; / And He has not hidden His face from him; / But when he cried to Him for help, He heard.
Who Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that having died to sin, we might live to righteousness; by His wounds you were healed.

left.text: And he threw the pieces of silver into the sanctuary and departed; and he went away and hanged himself. And the chief priests took the pieces of silver and said, “It is not lawful to put them into the temple treasury, since it is the price of blood.”

right.text: You shall not bring the hire of a harlot or the wages of a dog into the house of Yahweh your God for any votive offering, for both of these are an abomination to Yahweh your God.

lines.text: 'I have sinned by betraying innocent blood' (27:4): a plea, a confession, or both? We are not told.
The leaders will not put blood money in the treasury, yet carry out the plot that produced it: an odd duality of wickedness and ceremony, close to Jesus' teaching on hypocrisy.

left.text: Then that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying, “And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one whose price had been set by the sons of Israel; and they gave them for the Potter’s Field, as the Lord directed me.”

right.text: Then Yahweh said to me, “Throw it to the potter, that valuable price at which I was valued by them.” So I took the thirty shekels of silver and threw them to the potter in the house of Yahweh.

lines.text: Judas throws the silver into the sanctuary because, even in betrayal, he knows his Scripture. Thirty shekels was the price of a slave (Exodus 21:32): an insult.
Matthew names Jeremiah; the video suggests Jeremiah 19:1-13, with the potter's jar and the blood of the innocent.

src.text: Now Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned Him, saying, “Are You the King of the Jews?” And Jesus said to him, “You yourself say it.” And while He was being accused by the chief priests and elders, He did not answer.

lines.text: A commentator reads 'You yourself say it' as 'that's your way of putting it.' Jesus is King and Son of God, but not as Pilate or Caiaphas understand it; He rejects their framing while answering yes.
His silence again fulfills Isaiah 53:7, as before the chief priests.

src.text: Now when Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but rather that a riot was starting, he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of this man’s blood; see to that yourselves.” And all the people answered and said, “His blood be on us and on our children!”

lines.text: Pilate knew it was envy (27:18). The chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds (27:20). Barabbas means 'son of a father'; Mark says he was held with insurrectionists (Mark 15:7). Son of a father against the Son of the heavenly Father.

'His blood be on us' echoes the law's phrase 'His bloodguiltiness is upon him' (Leviticus 20:9): taking full responsibility. Many see it fulfilled in AD 70, but no one should see a curse on all Jews for all time; it concerns 'this evil generation' (12:45; 23:36).

left.text: And when they had crucified Him, they divided up His garments among themselves by casting lots.

right.text: They divide my garments among them, / And for my clothing they cast lots.

lines.text: The wine mixed with gall is bitter myrrh (Mark 15:23), which would have dulled the pain; He would not drink. The custom may rest on Proverbs 31:6; Matthew may also see Psalm 69:21.
The mockers' 'He trusts in God; let God rescue Him' matches Psalm 22:7-8. Jesus had told the disciples all of this in advance (20:18-19).

left.text: And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?” that is, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

right.text: All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to Yahweh, / And all the families of the nations will worship before You.

lines.text: The cry is a remez, a hint that sends hearers to the whole psalm, which ends in victory: 'He has done it' (Psalm 22:31). In His death Jesus is still teaching. Compare His last word in John: 'It is finished!' (John 19:30).
The darkness recalls Joel 2:10, just before the promise of the Spirit that Peter quotes at Pentecost (Acts 2).

CROSS.title: The veil, the tombs, the grave

left.text: And behold, the veil of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom; and the earth shook and the rocks were split.

right.text: So His grave was assigned with wicked men, / Yet He was with a rich man in His death, / Because He had done no violence, / Nor was there any deceit in His mouth.

lines.text: Which veil? One divided the holy place from the holy of holies, another the holy place from the courts. Either spells doom for the temple; Jesus Himself is the true temple. The video leaves the raised saints (27:52-53) as an open question.
The earthquake echoes 1 Kings 19:11, Isaiah 29:6, Jeremiah 10:10 and Ezekiel 26:18. Joseph, a rich man, buries Him (Isaiah 53:9).

BACKGROUND.p: Rome reserved crucifixion for slaves, rebels and the worst criminals. Scourging came first; the condemned often carried the crossbeam, and a placard named the charge.
Pilate normally lived in Caesarea and came to Jerusalem at the feasts to keep order. A stone found at Caesarea in 1961 names him prefect of Judea.
Wealthy families cut tombs into the rock, closed with a large stone. Burial had to happen before the Sabbath began at sunset.

WITNESSES.text: This cry rent the veil, and opened the tombs, and made the house desolate.

WITNESSES.text: Eighty and six years have I served Him, and He never did me any injury: how then can I blaspheme my King and my Saviour?

DEBATES.p: Most think the inner veil before the holy of holies (Hebrews 10:19-20); some the outer curtain, visible to all. The video leaves it open.
Some read 27:52-53 as a literal event; others as apocalyptic imagery woven into the narrative. The video says it is still weighing this.
Many hold that the Son bore the Father's judgment and in that sense was forsaken. The video stresses that the cry points to the whole psalm, which ends in God's answer (Psalm 22:21, 24).

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: Caiaphas asked whether Jesus is 'the Christ, the Son of God' (26:63); 'King of the Jews' is Pilate's question (27:11).
'His blood be on us' is Matthew 27:25, not 27:2.
The burial is 27:57-61 and the guard 27:62-66; the video gives verses 55 to 60.
'Jesus Barabbas' appears in only some manuscripts of 27:16-17; most English Bibles, including the LSB, read 'Barabbas.'

QUESTIONS: What might Matthew be implying with the triad of Judas, Pilate and the crowd?
Why did the leaders refuse the blood money but not the plot?
How does reading all of Psalm 22 change how you hear 'My God, My God'?
Which veil do you think was torn, and what difference does it make?
How did Stephen, Peter and Polycarp show they had learned from Jesus how to die?
What would it look like for you to be so filled with God's word that it flows out at the end?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: The cross first means that Jesus bore our sins in His body (1 Peter 2:24); we never outgrow justification and atonement. But there is a lesson for disciples too: set free from the law of sin and of death (Romans 8:2), the apostles were also free to die, and Stephen, Peter and Polycarp died on their Savior's model. Death, like suffering, is appointed by God for a purpose. The lesson: dying is the final act of obedience that a person can perform unto God, and the one who is filled with the word of God will glorify God in their final act of obedience. God did not forsake Jesus, and He will not forsake His people.

   (video) 'I have sinned by betraying innocent blood' (27:4): a plea, a confession, or both? We are not told.

## Key people
- Pilate: Knows it is envy, washes his hands: one of the triad who shed innocent blood. [Background] Roman prefect of Judea, AD 26-36.
- Barabbas: A notorious prisoner, probably a zealot; 'son of a father.' [Background] Some manuscripts of 27:16-17 call him Jesus Barabbas.
- Judas: Remorseful, returns the silver, throws it into the sanctuary. [Background] Acts 1:18-19 gives another account of his death and the Field of Blood.
- Simon of Cyrene: Pressed into service to bear the cross. [Background] Mark names his sons, Alexander and Rufus (Mark 15:21).
- The centurion: Sees the earthquake and confesses, 'Truly this was God's Son!' [Background] A Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers.
- Joseph of Arimathea: A rich man and disciple who buries Jesus in his own new tomb. [Background] A member of the council (Mark 15:43).

## Places [Background]
- Temple (named in the video): Judas 'threw the pieces of silver into the sanctuary' (27:5).
- Praetorium (traditional): Where the soldiers mocked Jesus (27:27).
- Golgotha (traditional) (named in the video): 'A place called Golgotha, which means Place of a Skull' (27:33).

## Key terms
- Golgotha: Aramaic for 'Place of a Skull,' outside Jerusalem's wall.
- Remez: A hint: quoting part of a passage to call the whole to mind.
- Day of Preparation: The day before the Sabbath, that is, Friday.
- Veil: The curtain in the sanctuary; the inner one screened the holy of holies.

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Roman crucifixion: Rome reserved crucifixion for slaves, rebels and the worst criminals. Scourging came first; the condemned often carried the crossbeam, and a placard named the charge.
- The governor at Passover: Pilate normally lived in Caesarea and came to Jerusalem at the feasts to keep order. A stone found at Caesarea in 1961 names him prefect of Judea.
- Rock-cut tombs: Wealthy families cut tombs into the rock, closed with a large stone. Burial had to happen before the Sabbath began at sunset.

## Early witnesses [Background: sourced]
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "This cry rent the veil, and opened the tombs, and made the house desolate." Homilies on Matthew 88, on 27:50-51. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).
- Martyrdom of Polycarp (c. AD 156): "Eighty and six years have I served Him, and He never did me any injury: how then can I blaspheme my King and my Saviour?" Martyrdom of Polycarp 9. ANF 1 (public domain). The video names Polycarp as one who died well.

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Which veil was torn? Most think the inner veil before the holy of holies (Hebrews 10:19-20); some the outer curtain, visible to all. The video leaves it open.
- The raised saints Some read 27:52-53 as a literal event; others as apocalyptic imagery woven into the narrative. The video says it is still weighing this.
- Forsaken? Many hold that the Son bore the Father's judgment and in that sense was forsaken. The video stresses that the cry points to the whole psalm, which ends in God's answer (Psalm 22:21, 24).

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- Caiaphas asked whether Jesus is 'the Christ, the Son of God' (26:63); 'King of the Jews' is Pilate's question (27:11).
- 'His blood be on us' is Matthew 27:25, not 27:2.
- The burial is 27:57-61 and the guard 27:62-66; the video gives verses 55 to 60.
- 'Jesus Barabbas' appears in only some manuscripts of 27:16-17; most English Bibles, including the LSB, read 'Barabbas.'

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. What might Matthew be implying with the triad of Judas, Pilate and the crowd?
2. Why did the leaders refuse the blood money but not the plot?
3. How does reading all of Psalm 22 change how you hear 'My God, My God'?
4. Which veil do you think was torn, and what difference does it make?
5. How did Stephen, Peter and Polycarp show they had learned from Jesus how to die?
6. What would it look like for you to be so filled with God's word that it flows out at the end?

## Application
- (video) The cross first means that Jesus bore our sins in His body (1 Peter 2:24); we never outgrow justification and atonement. But there is a lesson for disciples too: set free from the law of sin and of death (Romans 8:2), the apostles were also free to die, and Stephen, Peter and Polycarp died on their Savior's model. Death, like suffering, is appointed by God for a purpose. The lesson: dying is the final act of obedience that a person can perform unto God, and the one who is filled with the word of God will glorify God in their final act of obedience. God did not forsake Jesus, and He will not forsake His people.
- Study note (added): read Psalm 22 aloud this week, and choose one verse from its second half to memorize.
